sections.heading: One place short of the gold places
sections.text: mtg rises from twenty-second to seventeenth against the previous evening comparison, adding 3.48 points to reach 69.31. The provisional gold score is 69.44: the gap is less than a fifth of a point. It is a consequential late advance in the medal chase, even though it leaves mtg outside the gold places at this cutoff.

sections.heading: Tufa holds the summit
sections.text: Tufa Labs remains first on 88.06, followed by Yi-Chia Chen @ Fields Model on 84.72 and Domdolus Tolus on 82.08. nvbanana holds fourth on 81.39 and rabbithole fifth on 80.83. None of these five has a score gain in the edition’s comparison. Chen’s separate ARC3 lead does not change this contest’s order.

sections.heading: Pressure spreads below the leaders
sections.text: Enes Kulak adds 2.78 points to reach nineteenth on 68.89; ARC Raiders falls from eighteenth to twentieth with its score unchanged at 68.75. Yanming (Owen) Dong gains nearly ten points to reach 61.53 and thirty-first, while Nguyen reaches thirtieth on 61.94. The latter is team 16600664, a separate entry from the Thanh Hau Nguyen roster account named in the desk’s outstanding research assignment. Scores establish progress, not the methods behind it. The closing snapshot also records megsub jumping from 41.25 to 56.25 and from 67th to 39th in that individual score event; that event is not a separately established full-day comparison.

sections.heading: Read the wire windows carefully
sections.text: The morning wire recorded kibuna reaching twentieth on 67.22. Its Kaz report described a rise from 169th to 73rd over that report’s rolling window; the edition comparison instead has Kaz moving from 79th to 73rd, adding 2.64 to reach the same 40.14. The afternoon wire recorded poge0593 moving from 1,531st to 89th on 36.94. Those reports document the broader field’s movement without turning an earlier observation into a fresh evening gain.

sections.heading: Final selections still need attention
sections.text: In the public discussion saved by the desk on October 27, Kaggle staff María Cruz says runs submitted before the November 2 deadline can continue scoring afterward, but a pending run must be selected among the two final submissions before that deadline. The same saved discussion says the grand-prize criterion uses the private board. This is dated staff guidance, not a fresh announcement or a promise based on today’s public scores. Social and discussion research was not refreshed for this edition. All public medal positions remain provisional.

discussionThreads.reason: Staff reply and follow-ups verified without login. Actual cited X announcement inspected; no explicit public/private wording there.
discussionThreads.summary: Kaggle staff María Cruz says on October 23 at 23:39 UTC that submissions made before November 2 at 23:59 UTC keep scoring afterward, but a pending run must be selected among the two final submissions before the deadline. Private standings appear after all pre-deadline queued runs finish; the later winners announcement follows verification. Cruz says the 85% grand-prize criterion uses the private board and invites Greg Kamradt to clarify. Participants question consistency with ARC Prize’s October 9 bonus-prize announcement. The desk checked that actual X post: it promises a split among teams above 85% but does not explicitly name public or private. Participant inference is not a confirmed contradiction.

The rise puts Kaz inside the board's top 100, a substantial climb in a field of 3,423 teams.
